category: Image Processing Toolbox > Filtering, Enhancement & Morphology
description: Linear and nonlinear spatial filters, edge and gradient operators, denoising, sharpening, and the binary and grayscale morphology operators built on structuring elements.

tools.name: imfilter
tools.description: Apply a multidimensional correlation or convolution filter to an image with explicit control over boundary handling and output size. Unlike conv2 it preserves the input class and offers replicate/symmetric/circular padding, which avoids dark borders. It is the general-purpose linear filtering function for images.
tools.usage:
B = imfilter(A, h)
B = imfilter(A, h, options, ...)

parameters.name: 'replicate'/'symmetric'/'circular'/scalar
parameters.description: Boundary padding option; default pads with 0.

tools.notes: imfilter saturates integer results rather than wrapping. Convert to double first if you need signed outputs such as gradients.

tools.name: fspecial
tools.description: Create a predefined 2-D filter kernel: averaging, disk, Gaussian, Laplacian, Laplacian-of-Gaussian, motion blur, Prewitt or Sobel. It is the standard source of kernels for imfilter and conv2. Each type has its own size and shape parameters.
tools.usage:
h = fspecial(type)
h = fspecial('average', hsize)
h = fspecial('gaussian', hsize, sigma)
h = fspecial('motion', len, theta)
h = fspecial('log', hsize, sigma)

parameters.name: len, theta
parameters.description: Motion blur length in pixels and angle in degrees.

tools.notes: fspecial3 creates 3-D kernels for volumes. For Gaussian smoothing prefer imgaussfilt, which is separable and faster.

tools.name: imgaussfilt
tools.description: Filter an image with a 2-D Gaussian kernel specified by its standard deviation, using a fast separable implementation. It is the preferred way to blur or smooth an image because it is isotropic, has no ringing, and scales well. Filter size defaults to 2*ceil(2*sigma)+1 and can be overridden.
tools.usage:
B = imgaussfilt(A)
B = imgaussfilt(A, sigma)
B = imgaussfilt(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Standard deviation in pixels; scalar or [sx sy] for anisotropic smoothing (default 0.5).

tools.notes: imgaussfilt3 handles volumes. For edge-preserving smoothing use imbilatfilt or imdiffusefilt instead.

tools.name: medfilt2
tools.description: Apply a 2-D median filter over a sliding neighbourhood. It removes salt-and-pepper noise very effectively while keeping edges sharp, which linear filters cannot do. Larger neighbourhoods remove more noise but start to erode fine structures.
tools.usage:
B = medfilt2(A)
B = medfilt2(A, [m n])
B = medfilt2(___, padopt)
tools.notes: Only operates on 2-D grayscale data; filter colour images channel-by-channel or convert to YCbCr first.

tools.name: ordfilt2
tools.description: Two-dimensional order-statistic filter: replace each pixel with the nth smallest value in a specified neighbourhood. Choosing n = 1 gives a minimum (erosion-like) filter, n = numel gives a maximum, and the middle gives a median. Use it for rank-based morphology with arbitrary neighbourhood shapes.
tools.usage:
B = ordfilt2(A, order, domain)
B = ordfilt2(A, order, domain, S)
B = ordfilt2(___, padopt)

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Which order statistic to select, 1 to nnz(domain).

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Logical matrix defining the neighbourhood shape.

parameters.name: S
parameters.description: Additive offsets the same size as domain (for grayscale morphology).

tools.name: wiener2
tools.description: Adaptive Wiener noise-removal filter that estimates local mean and variance in a neighbourhood and smooths more where the variance is low. This preserves edges better than uniform smoothing because it leaves high-variance regions largely intact. Best suited to additive constant-power noise such as Gaussian.
tools.usage:
J = wiener2(I)
J = wiener2(I, [m n])
[J, noise] = wiener2(I, [m n], noise)

parameters.name: noise
parameters.description: Noise variance; estimated automatically if omitted.

tools.name: imsharpen
tools.description: Sharpen an image using an unsharp-masking algorithm: subtract a Gaussian-blurred copy and add the scaled difference back. Radius controls the size of the detail enhanced and Amount controls its strength. A Threshold prevents low-contrast noise from being amplified.
tools.usage:
B = imsharpen(A)
B = imsharpen(A, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Radius'
parameters.description: Standard deviation of the Gaussian lowpass (default 1).

parameters.name: 'Amount'
parameters.description: Strength of the enhancement (default 0.8); typical values 0.5-2.

parameters.name: 'Threshold'
parameters.description: 0 to 1 minimum contrast for a pixel to be sharpened (default 0).

tools.name: imbilatfilt
tools.description: Edge-preserving bilateral filter that weights neighbours by both spatial distance and intensity difference. Pixels across a strong edge contribute little, so noise is smoothed while edges stay sharp. Use it as a cartoon-like denoiser or as a preprocessing step before segmentation.
tools.usage:
B = imbilatfilt(I)
B = imbilatfilt(I, degreeOfSmoothing)
B = imbilatfilt(I, degreeOfSmoothing, spatialSigma)
B = imbilatfilt(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: degreeOfSmoothing
parameters.description: Intensity-range variance; larger smooths across bigger intensity differences.

tools.name: imdiffusefilt
tools.description: Anisotropic (Perona-Malik) diffusion filtering, which iteratively smooths within regions while inhibiting diffusion across edges. The conduction method and gradient threshold control how strongly edges are preserved. Classic choice for denoising medical and ultrasound images.
tools.usage:
B = imdiffusefilt(I)
B = imdiffusefilt(I, Name, Value)
[gradThresh, numIter] = imdiffuseest(I)

parameters.name: 'GradientThreshold'
parameters.description: Scalar or per-iteration vector controlling edge sensitivity.

tools.name: imnlmfilt
tools.description: Non-local means denoising: average each pixel with others whose surrounding patches look similar, no matter where they are in the image. It preserves repetitive texture far better than local filters at the price of substantially more computation. Often the best general-purpose classical denoiser.
tools.usage:
B = imnlmfilt(I)
B = imnlmfilt(I, Name, Value)
[B, estDoS] = imnlmfilt(___)

parameters.name: 'DegreeOfSmoothing'
parameters.description: Controls how aggressively similar patches are averaged; estimated automatically by default.

parameters.name: 'SearchWindowSize'
parameters.description: Odd size of the region searched for similar patches (default 21).

parameters.name: 'ComparisonWindowSize'
parameters.description: Odd patch size used for similarity (default 5).

tools.name: edge
tools.description: Detect edges in a grayscale or binary image using Sobel, Prewitt, Roberts, Laplacian-of-Gaussian, zero-cross or Canny methods. Canny is usually the most robust because it uses hysteresis thresholding and non-maximum suppression. Returns a binary edge map and optionally the thresholds actually used.
tools.usage:
BW = edge(I)
BW = edge(I, method)
BW = edge(I, method, threshold)
BW = edge(I, 'canny', threshold, sigma)
[BW, threshOut] = edge(___)

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: Scalar, or [low high] for Canny hysteresis; [] lets MATLAB choose.

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Gaussian standard deviation for 'canny' (default sqrt(2)) and 'log' (default 2).

tools.name: imgradient
tools.description: Compute the gradient magnitude and direction of an image using a chosen operator. Unlike edge it returns continuous-valued maps rather than a binary decision, which is what watershed, active contours and feature detectors need. Several kernels are available including Sobel, Prewitt, Roberts, central and intermediate differences.
tools.usage:
[Gmag, Gdir] = imgradient(I)
[Gmag, Gdir] = imgradient(I, method)
[Gmag, Gdir] = imgradient(Gx, Gy)
tools.notes: Gdir is in degrees in (-180, 180], measured counterclockwise from the positive x-axis.

tools.name: imgradientxy
tools.description: Compute the directional derivatives of an image along x and y with a chosen operator. Its outputs feed directly into imgradient, or can be used to build structure tensors and orientation histograms. Returned as double (or single) so signed values are preserved.
tools.usage:
[Gx, Gy] = imgradientxy(I)
[Gx, Gy] = imgradientxy(I, method)

tools.name: strel
tools.description: Create a morphological structuring element of a given shape and size. The shape determines which neighbours a morphological operation looks at, so it controls what features survive erosion, dilation, opening and closing. Many shapes decompose into smaller elements automatically, making operations much faster.
tools.usage:
SE = strel(nhood)
SE = strel('disk', r)
SE = strel('disk', r, n)
SE = strel('line', len, deg)
SE = strel('rectangle', [m n])
SE = strel('square', w)
SE = strel('diamond', r)

parameters.name: 'disk', r
parameters.description: Disk of radius r; n (0, 4, 6 or 8) controls the polygon approximation.

parameters.name: 'line', len, deg
parameters.description: Linear element of given length and angle in degrees.

parameters.name: nhood
parameters.description: A logical matrix giving an arbitrary custom neighbourhood.

tools.notes: offsetstrel creates non-flat (grayscale) structuring elements such as balls, used for rolling-ball background subtraction.

tools.name: imerode
tools.description: Morphologically erode an image, shrinking bright regions by the shape of the structuring element. In binary images it removes small objects and thins shapes; in grayscale it is a local minimum filter. Use it to separate touching objects or to strip away noise specks.
tools.usage:
J = imerode(I, SE)
J = imerode(I, nhood)
J = imerode(___, packopt, m)

parameters.name: SE
parameters.description: A strel or offsetstrel object, or an array of them applied in sequence.

tools.name: imdilate
tools.description: Morphologically dilate an image, growing bright regions by the structuring element shape. It fills small holes and gaps, connects nearby components and thickens features. In grayscale it acts as a local maximum filter.
tools.usage:
J = imdilate(I, SE)
J = imdilate(I, nhood)
J = imdilate(___, packopt, m)

parameters.name: SE
parameters.description: strel/offsetstrel object or array of them.

tools.name: imopen
tools.description: Morphological opening: erosion followed by dilation with the same structuring element. It removes small bright objects and thin protrusions while leaving the size and shape of larger objects essentially intact. The classic use is estimating a slowly varying background for subtraction.
tools.usage:
J = imopen(I, SE)
J = imopen(I, nhood)

parameters.name: SE
parameters.description: Structuring element; must be larger than the features you want removed.

tools.name: imclose
tools.description: Morphological closing: dilation followed by erosion with the same structuring element. It fills small dark holes and narrow gaps inside bright objects without noticeably growing them. Often used to repair broken object boundaries before labelling.
tools.usage:
J = imclose(I, SE)
J = imclose(I, nhood)

parameters.name: SE
parameters.description: Structuring element sized to the gaps you want to close.

tools.name: imtophat
tools.description: Top-hat transform: the original image minus its morphological opening, which isolates bright features smaller than the structuring element. It is the standard one-step correction for uneven illumination. Use a structuring element larger than the objects you want to keep.
tools.usage:
J = imtophat(I, SE)
J = imtophat(I, nhood)

parameters.name: SE
parameters.description: Structuring element larger than the bright features of interest.

tools.name: imbothat
tools.description: Bottom-hat (black top-hat) transform: the morphological closing minus the original image, which isolates dark features smaller than the structuring element. Combining top-hat and bottom-hat is a common contrast-enhancement recipe. Use it when your objects of interest are darker than the background.
tools.usage:
J = imbothat(I, SE)
J = imbothat(I, nhood)

parameters.name: SE
parameters.description: Structuring element larger than the dark features of interest.

tools.name: bwmorph
tools.description: Apply a named morphological operation to a binary image, such as skeletonizing, thinning, spurring, bridging, cleaning or finding branch points. Dozens of classical operations are packed into one function with an optional repeat count. Use 'inf' as the count to iterate until the result stops changing.
tools.usage:
BW2 = bwmorph(BW, operation)
BW2 = bwmorph(BW, operation, n)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of times to apply the operation, or Inf to iterate to stability.

tools.notes: For skeletonization bwskel is newer, supports 3-D, and has a MinBranchLength option.

tools.name: bwskel
tools.description: Reduce binary objects to a one-pixel-wide centerline skeleton while preserving topology, in 2-D or 3-D. The MinBranchLength option prunes short spurious spurs, which are the usual nuisance of skeletonization. Use it for vessel, crack and road network analysis.
tools.usage:
out = bwskel(A)
out = bwskel(V)
out = bwskel(___, 'MinBranchLength', n)

parameters.name: 'MinBranchLength'
parameters.description: Branches shorter than this many pixels are removed (default 0).

tools.name: imfill
tools.description: Fill holes in a binary or grayscale image, where a hole is a region that cannot be reached from the image border. The 'holes' option fills all of them at once; supplying seed locations fills only connected regions from those points. Essential after thresholding when objects come out hollow.
tools.usage:
BW2 = imfill(BW, 'holes')
BW2 = imfill(BW, locations)
BW2 = imfill(BW, conn, 'holes')
I2 = imfill(I, 'holes')
BW2 = imfill(BW)

parameters.name: 'holes'
parameters.description: Fill every hole not connected to the image border.

parameters.name: locations
parameters.description: Linear indices or n-by-ndims subscripts of seed points.

tools.name: imclearborder
tools.description: Remove objects that touch the border of a binary image (or suppress border-connected structures in grayscale). Objects clipped by the field of view give unreliable size and shape measurements, so discarding them is standard practice. Connectivity controls which neighbours count as touching.
tools.usage:
J = imclearborder(I)
J = imclearborder(I, conn)

tools.name: bwareaopen
tools.description: Remove connected components with fewer than a given number of pixels from a binary image. It is the simplest and most common way to delete speckle noise after thresholding. Connectivity can be set to 4 or 8 (or 6/18/26 in 3-D).
tools.usage:
BW2 = bwareaopen(BW, P)
BW2 = bwareaopen(BW, P, conn)

parameters.name: P
parameters.description: Minimum number of pixels an object must have to be kept.

tools.notes: bwareafilt is more flexible: it can keep the n largest objects or a size range.

tools.name: bwareafilt
tools.description: Keep only the binary objects whose areas fall in a given range, or the n largest or smallest objects. It is more expressive than bwareaopen because it can select by rank as well as by threshold. Ties are broken by the tie-breaking option.
tools.usage:
BW2 = bwareafilt(BW, range)
BW2 = bwareafilt(BW, n)
BW2 = bwareafilt(BW, n, keep)
BW2 = bwareafilt(___, conn)

tools.name: bwdist
tools.description: Compute the Euclidean (or city-block, chessboard, quasi-Euclidean) distance transform of a binary image: for each pixel, the distance to the nearest nonzero pixel. It can also return the index of that nearest pixel, giving a nearest-neighbour map. It is the foundation of watershed-based object separation and of skeleton and shape analysis.
tools.usage:
D = bwdist(BW)
[D, idx] = bwdist(BW)
[D, idx] = bwdist(BW, method)

parameters.name: BW
parameters.description: Binary image; distances are measured to the nearest true pixel.

tools.name: imreconstruct
tools.description: Morphological reconstruction: repeatedly dilate a marker image under a mask image until stability. It is the engine behind imfill, imclearborder and h-minima transforms, and lets you select whole objects from seed points without changing their shape. A key tool for extracting connected structures exactly.
tools.usage:
J = imreconstruct(marker, mask)
J = imreconstruct(marker, mask, conn)

parameters.name: marker
parameters.description: Seed image; must be element-wise less than or equal to mask.

tools.name: imextendedmax
tools.description: Find extended maxima: connected regions whose intensity is at least h greater than all surrounding pixels. It filters out shallow local maxima caused by noise, returning a clean binary marker image. Commonly used to seed marker-controlled watershed segmentation.
tools.usage:
BW = imextendedmax(I, H)
BW = imextendedmax(I, H, conn)

parameters.name: H
parameters.description: Height threshold; larger values keep only more prominent maxima.

tools.notes: imextendedmin, imhmax, imhmin and imimposemin are the related h-transform family.

tools.name: imimposemin
tools.description: Modify an image so that its only regional minima are at specified marker locations. Applying it before watershed is the standard cure for over-segmentation, because each marker becomes exactly one catchment basin. Combine with imextendedmax or manually placed seeds.
tools.usage:
I2 = imimposemin(I, BW)
I2 = imimposemin(I, BW, conn)

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Grayscale image, typically a gradient magnitude.

parameters.name: BW
parameters.description: Binary marker image; true pixels become the forced minima.

tools.name: deconvwnr
tools.description: Deblur an image by Wiener deconvolution given the point spread function and a noise-to-signal power ratio. It is the fastest and most stable of the classical deconvolution methods when the PSF is known. Too small an NSR amplifies noise into ringing, too large leaves the image blurred.
tools.usage:
J = deconvwnr(I, psf)
J = deconvwnr(I, psf, nsr)
J = deconvwnr(I, psf, ncorr, icorr)

parameters.name: psf
parameters.description: Point spread function that caused the blur.

parameters.name: nsr
parameters.description: Noise-to-signal power ratio, scalar or array (default 0).

parameters.name: ncorr, icorr
parameters.description: Autocorrelation functions of the noise and the undegraded image.

tools.notes: deconvlucy (Richardson-Lucy), deconvreg and deconvblind cover iterative, regularized and unknown-PSF cases.

tools.name: deconvblind
tools.description: Blind deconvolution: simultaneously estimate the deblurred image and the point spread function from an initial PSF guess. Use it when the blur kernel is unknown, supplying only an estimate of its size. The quality of the initial PSF size guess strongly affects the result.
tools.usage:
[J, psfr] = deconvblind(I, psfi)
[J, psfr] = deconvblind(I, psfi, iter)
[J, psfr] = deconvblind(I, psfi, iter, dampar, weight)

parameters.name: psfi
parameters.description: Initial PSF estimate; its size matters more than its values.

parameters.name: dampar
parameters.description: Damping threshold to suppress noise amplification.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: Per-pixel weight array to exclude bad pixels.

tools.name: imlocalbrighten
tools.description: Brighten the dark regions of a low-light image using a dehazing-based local model, leaving already-bright regions largely unchanged. The amount parameter controls the strength and an alpha-blending option preserves natural appearance. Use it as a one-line fix for underexposed photographs.
tools.usage:
B = imlocalbrighten(A)
B = imlocalbrighten(A, amount)
[B, D] = imlocalbrighten(___, 'AlphaBlend', true)

parameters.name: 'AlphaBlend'
parameters.description: Logical; blend the brightened result with the original to avoid over-processing.

tools.name: imreducehaze
tools.description: Reduce atmospheric haze in an image using a dark-channel or approximate dehazing method. It restores contrast and colour saturation in outdoor and aerial imagery. The optional second output returns the estimated transmission map, which is itself a rough depth cue.
tools.usage:
B = imreducehaze(A)
B = imreducehaze(A, amount)
[B, T, L] = imreducehaze(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'AtmosphericLight'
parameters.description: Manually specified atmospheric light per channel.
